name: cardgame-jaina-sync-scope-conflict-note
title: Flag the tools/sync-cards-to-jaina.js scope conflict before both queued units build
pitch: Two units already sitting in the 12-deep ready queue — cardgame-jaina-card-sync-dryrun and cardgame-sync-cards-to-jaina — both claim tools/sync-cards-to-jaina.js with incompatible acceptance criteria (dry-run print-only vs. live mocked-upsert); file a mechanical conflict note now instead of letting them collide mid-build.
why_now: The ready queue is 12 deep and every recent tick added cardgame units without pruning any — exactly the 'roadmap only grew' case where portfolio rules call for a deletion/simplification candidate. Reading units/cardgame-jaina-card-sync-dryrun/unit.md and units/cardgame-sync-cards-to-jaina/unit.md side by side shows both target the same output path with different contracts: one is a network-free stdout dry-run, the other requires a mocked Jaina client and upsert-by-call-count assertions. If both get promoted and built as-is, the second to land silently overwrites or contradicts the first's tests. T13 already vetoed one duplicate-proposal case as 'overlap-guard bait, one unit suffices' — this is the same shape, caught before either burns a build cycle.
expected_outcome: design/tooling-conflicts.md exists, names both units by their exact unit names, documents the same-file/incompatible-criteria conflict, and contains the literal marker 'NEEDS ROUTERBOX DECISION' — readable and actionable at the next walkthrough in under a minute.
intent: units/cardgame-jaina-card-sync-dryrun/unit.md and units/cardgame-sync-cards-to-jaina/unit.md are both currently ready-to-build and both specify tools/sync-cards-to-jaina.js as their primary deliverable, but with mutually exclusive behavior: the dryrun unit's AC3 requires the script to print a 'not yet implemented' message and exit 1 when run without --dry-run, while the sync unit requires that same invocation to perform a live (mocked-in-test) upsert. Per T11, a pure repo-state cleanup or silent pick-a-winner unit cannot pass TDD honestly and isn't the Producer's call to make — the right shape is an investigation-only unit that surfaces the conflict by name for RouterBox to resolve via the normal promote/veto gate, not a new ad-hoc escalation mechanism. This unit adds design/tooling-conflicts.md, a short mechanical document naming both units, quoting the specific contradicting acceptance criteria, and stating a suggested resolution (dryrun ships first as the narrower slice; sync-cards-to-jaina should be re-scoped to build on the dryrun's output rather than redefining the same script) while flagging the final call as unresolved. No cardgame design content, rules, or tooling code is touched.

criteria.text: design/tooling-conflicts.md exists and contains a section naming both cardgame-jaina-card-sync-dryrun and cardgame-sync-cards-to-jaina by their exact unit names

The document quotes or paraphrases the specific contradiction: both units specify tools/sync-cards-to-jaina.js as their deliverable, but one requires a network-free dry-run-only script (exit 1 without --dry-run) and the other requires a live/mocked upsert on the same invocation shape
The document contains the literal string 'NEEDS ROUTERBOX DECISION' so the open question is greppable and cannot be mistaken for a resolved decision

The document states a suggested (non-binding) resolution ordering — which unit's scope is recommended to ship first and how the other should be re-scoped to build on it rather than redefine the same file

veto_reason: Conflict is real and well caught, but a conflict-note unit is not needed: orchestrator resolved it directly � retired cardgame-sync-cards-to-jaina (ledger resolution:retired) in favor of the already-running dryrun unit; Producer re-files the live-sync step after dryrun merges, specced to extend the tool.
